incident: OpenMicrowave 'Arm did not reach desired position' stall on the door-opening pull arc
attempt_note: Second OpenMicrowave attempt of the run (a redo), Speed=high.
failure_mode: Post-execution endpoint check in kinova.py:729-734 -- move_cartesian_trajectory sends all 11 waypoints as ONE ExecuteWaypointTrajectory, then checks only whether the FINAL EE position is within 1 cm of the last waypoint. It was not, so it printed 'Arm did not reach desired position' and returned False. The real firmware abort reason (protective stop / joint limit / following error) is swallowed: kinova.py:247-256 treats ACTION_END and ACTION_ABORT identically. The executive (base.py:704-731) turned the False into a teleop hand-off ('joint limit/reachability' is its own generic guess, not a firmware code).
attributed_waypoint: 11 of 11 (final). Physically the arm stalled somewhere along the arc; only the endpoint is checked, so the exact stall waypoint is not in the logs and must be measured on replay.
defined_in: actions/open_door.py:217 open_microwave -> move_to_ee_pose_trajectory(handle_opening_poses['opening_waypoints']); waypoints generated at runtime from the perceived handle by perception_interface.py:646 _generate_door_arc_waypoints (constant-z planar door arc, so these values are specific to this run's handle detection).

preamble.comment: Commands the arm server received immediately before the failing arc (NUC pane). Replaying these puts the arm in the same starting configuration/IK branch. In free space (no microwave) the gripper simply closes on nothing; recreate_joint_limit.py notes this class of stall is kinematic and needs no door contact -- but if the real cause was the door physically resisting, a free-space replay will NOT reproduce it.
